pageCache.pageTitle: Progressive IB School in London | Liberty Woodland School
pageCache.text:
A Progressive IB School in London
Education designed for the world ahead
We believe education should prepare young people not simply to succeed at school, but to thrive in life. As an IB World School, we combine academic rigour with curiosity, creativity and learning that has purpose beyond the classroom.
Just as importantly, we protect joy, nurture wellbeing and help young people know themselves. They leave us with strong qualifications, but also the independence, resilience and confidence to navigate uncertainty, build meaningful relationships and create lives they genuinely enjoy.
Education for today's world
From the earliest years, children at Liberty learn through curiosity, play, exploration and meaningful experiences. As they grow, this develops into increasingly sophisticated inquiry, academic challenge and real-world projects, culminating in the International Baccalaureate.
Throughout, we protect time for childhood, relationships, movement, nature and joy, while taking wellbeing and emotional development every bit as seriously as academic progress. Young people learn to think critically, communicate, collaborate, solve problems and understand themselves.
They leave us with strong qualifications, but also with something harder to measure: the confidence, resilience, independence and sense of possibility to shape a life that is genuinely their own.
Learning that matters: a progressive approach to education
From Nursery onwards, learning at Liberty has purpose, relevance and meaning. Children begin by exploring through play, nature and their own curiosity; as they grow, this develops into increasingly ambitious inquiry, interdisciplinary learning and real-world projects.
By connecting knowledge to their own lives and the world around them, young people become genuinely invested in what they are learning. They want to ask better questions, find solutions, test ideas, create, rethink and keep going when something doesn't work.
This doesn't come at the expense of academic rigour. It strengthens it. Alongside deep knowledge and strong academic foundations, young people develop the creativity, critical thinking and problem-solving skills to use what they know - not simply remember it.
Each child who joins us takes on our academically rigorous and challenging education, delivered through an engaging and deeply fulfilling curriculum.
With a focus on wellbeing, self-discovery and environmentalism, we help each child grow into a citizen for the future, to innovate and drive impactful change in our world.
We encourage children to explore their curiosity and deepen their understanding of topics they find particularly interesting.
Our self-directed, student-led approach to learning aims to develop key skills including critical thinking, collaboration, and creativity.
Learn more about project-based learning
As an IB school, we help our students develop a wider understanding of the world around them.
Following the International Baccalaureate framework supports our secondary school students to build critical thinking skills and cultural awareness, ultimately helping them become responsible members of an increasingly interconnected world.
Learn more about the IB curriculum
Immersive, hands-on learning
Self-led and project-based
Building global perspectives through the IB
A happier way to grow up
Wellbeing isn't something we add to education. It shapes the environment we create for children every day.
In Primary, children move naturally between inspiring classrooms and our extensive outdoor spaces, with nature woven into the school day. They might take their learning outside, investigate the natural world, work on an ambitious project or simply have the space to run, play and breathe.
It creates an environment that is both academically purposeful and wonderfully joyful - one where movement, fresh air, freedom and connection to nature support children's wellbeing, curiosity and readiness to learn.
Across Liberty, wellbeing is built through strong relationships, emotional literacy and being deeply known. From the earliest years, children learn to recognise and understand their emotions, put words to how they feel and develop the tools to regulate themselves.
As they grow, this develops into greater self-awareness, independence and genuine resilience, protecting their wellbeing without protecting them from every difficulty. We want them to achieve highly, but we also want them to be happy: at school, and in the lives they build beyond it.
Wellbeing in Primary School
Wellbeing in Secondary School
Life at Liberty Woodland School
Joyful, purposeful and full of possibility, life at Liberty gives young people the space to learn, belong, explore and become themselves.
A supportive learning community
Areas we serve across London
Liberty Woodland School is located in Morden, though we welcome families from a range of locations in London including: Barnes, Cheam, Clapham, Dulwich, Fulham, Putney, Southfield, Streatham, Surbiton, Tooting, Wandsworth, Wimbledon
Unsure how you’d get here? We provide a private minibus service across London to help get your children to our school.
Our minibus schedule
Is Liberty Woodland School academically rigorous?
Absolutely. We believe children can love school, be happy and achieve highly - these things should strengthen one another, not compete.
Children build strong foundations in knowledge and core academic skills alongside the ability to think critically, question, investigate and apply what they know. As they grow, expectations become increasingly ambitious, leading into the International Baccalaureate in Secondary and Sixth Form.
Our approach isn't about making learning easier; it's about making it deeper, more meaningful and more effective.
How is Liberty Woodland School different from a traditional school?
We have questioned many of the assumptions about what school has to look like. Children still gain the knowledge, skills and qualifications that matter, but their education is about much more than preparing for the next test.
Learning has purpose and relevance, childhood is protected, wellbeing and emotional development are taken seriously, and young people are given opportunities to solve problems, create, take responsibility and discover what they are capable of.
We want them to leave Liberty with strong qualifications, and as strong humans.
What ages does Liberty Woodland School take?
Liberty is an independent school for young people from Nursery through to Sixth Form. Our youngest children begin with play, exploration and discovery; learning then becomes increasingly sophisticated, independent and academically demanding as they grow.
Each stage is designed around what young people need developmentally at that age, while one philosophy connects the whole journey from three to eighteen.
Is Liberty Woodland School a Forest School?
No. Liberty is an academically ambitious independent school with an unusually strong connection to nature and the outdoors. Particularly in Nursery and Primary, children move naturally between inspiring classrooms and our extensive outdoor spaces for learning, exploration, movement and play.
We believe children shouldn't have to choose between a rigorous education and a childhood with space, freedom and time in nature. At Liberty, they have both.
What is the International Baccalaureate, and why does Liberty Woodland School offer it?
The International Baccalaureate is a globally recognised approach to education that combines academic depth with inquiry, critical thinking and the ability to connect and apply knowledge.
It fits naturally with the education we have always believed in at Liberty: intellectually ambitious, internationally minded and relevant to the world beyond school. Students follow the IB Middle Years Programme in Secondary, progressing to the Diploma Programme in Sixth Form.
How does Liberty Woodland School support children's wellbeing?
Wellbeing is woven into everyday life at Liberty rather than treated as an add-on. Children are deeply known by the adults around them and, from the earliest years, develop emotional literacy: learning to recognise and understand their emotions and developing the tools to regulate themselves.
Relationships, belonging, movement and time in nature matter too. As children grow, we increasingly develop self-awareness, independence and genuine resilience - protecting their wellbeing without protecting them from every difficulty.
Most importantly, we want children to love coming to school.
How much does Liberty Woodland School cost?
Fees vary across Nursery, Primary, Secondary and Sixth Form. We aim to be completely transparent about the cost of a Liberty education, including what is included within our fees and the bursaries and financial support that may be available.
Full, up-to-date fee information can be found on our fees page.
Where is Liberty Woodland School located, and do you offer school transport?
Liberty is in Morden, South West London, within the beautiful surroundings of Morden Hall Park. Our Primary and Secondary schools are based in neighbouring buildings within the park, with our Sixth Form opening nearby in September 2027.
Families travel to us from across South West London, and we operate school minibuses to make that journey easier, with routes serving areas including Barnes, Fulham, Putney, Wimbledon, Southfields, and Wandsworth.
We are always open to adding more stops in different areas if there is sufficient demand. Speak to our Admissions team about current routes and stops.
How can I find out whether Liberty Woodland School is right for my child?
Come and experience it. Liberty can feel quite different from a conventional school, and the best way to understand it is to see children learning, meet the people who know them and experience the atmosphere for yourself.
Our Open Days and Stay & Play sessions give families a genuine insight into life at Liberty, as well as plenty of opportunity to ask the questions that matter to you.
Book a place at our open day.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head
As Head of School, I am delighted to introduce you to our dynamic and nurturing school. At Liberty Woodland, our goal is to cultivate confident, creative, and compassionate individuals who are well-prepared for the challenges and opportunities of the future.
We take pride in offering a balanced, child-centered education that focuses on the development of both academic excellence and essential life skills. Our approach encourages students to be critical thinkers, problem-solvers, and effective communicators. By fostering independence and resilience, we empower our students to take ownership of their learning and to approach new situations with curiosity and confidence.
At Liberty Woodland, we value character development as much as academic achievement. Our students are guided to be empathetic leaders who respect the perspectives of others and work collaboratively to make positive contributions to their communities. We prioritise social-emotional growth, helping children develop strong self-awareness, emotional intelligence, and a sense of responsibility toward others.
We are deeply committed to creating an environment where every child feels happy, valued, supported, and inspired to reach their full and unique potential. Through a rich, engaging curriculum that blends traditional academics with hands-on experiences, our students are encouraged to explore their passions, think creatively, and approach challenges with a growth mindset.
Thank you for taking the time to learn about Liberty Woodland School. We are excited to be part of your child’s educational journey and to work together in shaping the confident, capable, and compassionate leaders of tomorrow.
Read more about our school Vision, Mission and Aims.
Book a place at our open day.

Careers
At Liberty Woodland School we’re always open to hearing from exceptional educators who are passionate about reshaping the future of education.
As a small, independent progressive school with a strong focus on outdoor education, we are dedicated to fostering an environment where students are equipped with the skills and mindset to thrive in an ever-changing world. In our primary school, we use project-based learning to inspire curiosity and creativity, while our secondary students follow the International Baccalaureate (IB) program, preparing them to be global thinkers and leaders.
We work with passionate educators who lead by example, are driven to innovate, and are excited about working in a school which is reimagining education. If you’re committed to empowering students to become adaptable, forward-thinking individuals who are ready for anything, we would love to hear from you.
Join us in our mission to create a learning environment that prepares students not just for academic success, but for life.
We’re always on the lookout for passionate, progressive educators and team members who want to help shape the future of education.
All our current vacancies are listed on TES, where you can view details and apply directly. Please check our TES page regularly for new opportunities to join our inspiring team.
Get in touch with us to send us your details.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Children Are More Than Exam Results
pageCache.text:
Our Children Are More Than Exam Results
This week, children across the country will walk into exam halls carrying far more than pens and calculators.
They are carrying pressure. Expectation. Fear.The belief that these few hours might define who they are.
That should concern all of us.
Because somewhere along the way, we have normalised an education system that asks children to prove their intelligence in near-silence, in isolation, cut off from collaboration, conversation, curiosity and research, the very things that define learning in the real world.
No adult workplace functions like this.
Architects do not work without references.Doctors do not work without discussion.Business leaders do not solve problems without teams.Scientists do not succeed without research, experimentation and failure.
Real life is messy, collaborative and interconnected.
Yet we continue to tell children that the truest measure of their understanding is whether they can sit alone in a sports hall and retrieve information from memory under pressure.
The Problem With Defining Success by Exam Results
Exams have a place. Absolutely.
There is value in learning knowledge deeply. There is value in discipline, preparation and independent thinking. The ability to recall information matters.
But somewhere along the line, exams stopped being one form of assessment and became, for many children, the assessment. The dominant measure. The thing that overshadows everything else.
And that is where the problem begins.
Because when exam performance becomes the primary currency of success, we start reducing children down to numbers, grades and data points. We create systems that reward a very narrow type of learner, while quietly overlooking countless others whose strengths are harder to measure in timed conditions.
Not Every Strength Can Fit Into a Mark Scheme
Some children thrive in exams. Many do not.
That is not weakness or laziness. And it is certainly not a measure of intelligence.
Some children think brilliantly out loud. Some communicate best through practical application, creativity or discussion. Some are extraordinary collaborators, innovators and problem-solvers - gifts that rarely fit neatly into a mark scheme.
We say we want young people who can think critically, communicate effectively, adapt to change and contribute meaningfully to the world.
Then we assess them in ways that reward compliance, memorisation and endurance above all else.
That contradiction deserves challenging.
The Emotional Burden of Exams
Perhaps most concerning of all is the emotional cost.
You can see it everywhere this week.
Children unable to sleep.Children crying before school.Children convinced that one bad result could ruin their future.Children carrying levels of anxiety that should never become normalised in childhood.
And underneath so much of that anxiety is a heart-breaking belief: If I fail these exams, I fail as a person.
No child should grow up believing that.
What Exams Fail To Measure
The irony is that many of the qualities we value most in adulthood are the very things our assessment systems struggle to recognise. Creativity. Emotional intelligence. Leadership. Curiosity. Resilience. Collaboration. The ability to ask thoughtful questions. The confidence to challenge ideas. The courage to think differently.
These are the qualities that shape meaningful lives and healthy societies.
And yet too often, they sit outside the exam hall doors.
This is not an argument for abandoning exams altogether. It is an argument for balance. For humanity. For remembering that assessment should serve children, not the other way around.
How The Future of Education Could Look
A healthier education system would still include exams, but alongside broader and richer ways for children to demonstrate understanding. Projects. Portfolios. Presentations. Practical application. Long-term coursework. Collaborative problem-solving. Real-world learning. One of the many reasons we value the International Baccalaureate MYP is that it includes a richness of assessment.
Because understanding is not one-dimensional. And children are certainly not one-dimensional.
Education should not leave young people feeling broken at 16.
It should leave them feeling capable.Curious.Valued.Known.
This week especially, as children across the country sit SATs and GCSEs, they need to hear something far more important than “do well”.
You are already enough.
You are more than your results.
And the qualities that will shape your life, your kindness, your creativity, your courage, your ability to think, question, connect and keep going, cannot always be measured in an exam hall.
How Liberty Woodland School Challenges Traditional Education
At Liberty Woodland School, we offer a progressive approach to education for primary school and secondary school children across London. We believe that children should be taught with intention, and that learning should be fun, engaging, and meaningful to their lives.
As an International Baccalaureate school, we are committed to making sure children deeply understand a range of topics through project based and self-directed learning. They are given freedom over their learning, helping them build key academic and personal skills.
We value your child as an individual, rather than a number or a grade.
If you are looking for a different type of education for your child, visit us on an open day and discover what makes Liberty Woodland School so unique.

Nursery timetable
Our days have a predictable rhythm, giving children the security of knowing what will happen while leaving plenty of time for exploration and uninterrupted play. Morning Meeting, shared meals, snacks and end-of-day reflection provide calm points of connection; the spaces between allow children’s concentration, creativity and learning to unfold.
Welcome and breakfast
Reflection and story
Between these familiar points, children enjoy extended periods of indoor and outdoor play, responsive teaching and carefully planned experiences shaped by their interests and developmental needs.
Return to Nursery homepage
Book a place at our open day.

Wellbeing
Wellbeing begins with being deeply known.
Our educators understand each child’s personality, communication, joys and difficulties, creating the emotional security and strong sense of belonging from which they can explore, connect and grow. We want every child to feel: “I am known. I belong.”
Deeply known and securely connected
Every child needs to feel that they belong and that there are trusted adults who will notice, understand and respond to them. Our small nursery enables close, consistent relationships in which children can feel completely safe to be themselves.
Developing emotional intelligence
Using the Zones of Regulation, children begin to notice what is happening in their bodies, recognise different emotions and find language for how they feel. Our educators co-regulate with them, gradually helping them understand what they need and develop the ability to regulate more independently.
Wellbeing rooted in nature
Spending most of the day outdoors gives children space to move, breathe, explore and reset. Nature, fresh air, physical movement and freedom from constant indoor stimulation help children feel calmer, more grounded and connected to the world around them.
Developing personalised toolkits
Breathing, mindfulness, movement and simple calming strategies are woven naturally into nursery life. Children gradually discover what helps them return to a place where they feel settled and ready to engage again.
A voice in their own day
Wellbeing also grows when children feel heard and experience a genuine sense of agency. Children have time to follow their interests, make choices, contribute ideas and influence their play - developing confidence in who they are and what they can do.
Resilience grows through experience
We do not build resilience by removing every difficulty. Through manageable challenge, supported risk, friendship struggles and everyday frustrations, children learn that they can persevere, recover, ask for help, fail and try again.
